report.summary: Chunk 2 of dss.py: prolongate_scores, TemporalEvidence, TemporalCarry, carry_temporal_scores, RelationChannel, _relation_adjacencies. Claims about projection, temporal carry, and relation diffusion are checked.
risks: _relation_adjacencies | high | The function's docstring claims 'DIFFUSION IS FILE-TO-FILE ONLY, BY CONSTRUCTION' but the implementation filters by file_ids, which is consistent. However, the claim about 2182 functions and 227 types is uncheckable. | Verify the forest data to confirm the numbers.

_relation_adjacencies | medium | The docstring claims 'Filtering by node KIND rather than by relation NAME is deliberate' but the code filters by file_ids, which is based on node kind. The claim is kept. | No action needed.

handoff.purpose: Defines Prolongation, prolongate_scores, TemporalEvidence, TemporalCarry, carry_temporal_scores, RelationChannel, and _relation_adjacencies.

symbols.name: Prolongation
symbols.note: Dataclass with file_scores, selected_hierarchy_nodes, pruned_hierarchy_nodes and to_dict method.

symbols.name: prolongate_scores
symbols.note: Projects restricted relevance down through at most branch_limit children per branch.

symbols.name: TemporalEvidence
symbols.note: Dataclass for temporal carry evidence with to_dict.

symbols.name: TemporalCarry
symbols.note: Dataclass with scores and evidence, to_dict method.

symbols.name: carry_temporal_scores
symbols.note: Carries old relevance through exact IDs and rename evidence.

symbols.name: RelationChannel
symbols.note: Dataclass for scores propagated through a relation, with to_dict.

claims.text: The restriction sum makes a child/parent ratio a deterministic share of incoming relevance.
claims.why: Code computes share = restricted_scores[child.id] / parent_score, then child_score = incoming * share.

claims.text: Pruned mass is not renormalised onto other branches; doing so would make a surviving low-score file appear more relevant merely because its sibling was removed.
claims.why: The function returns pruned nodes separately and does not redistribute their score.
In the loop, when previous_id in current_ids, confidence is set to 1.0.

claims.text: A rename mapping is considered only when the old ID no longer exists.
claims.why: Code checks if previous_id not in current_ids before using rename_map.

claims.text: Confidence is keyed by the old ID and defaults to 1 for a caller-asserted rename.
Multiple pieces of evidence targeting one file use ``max`` rather than summation to avoid artificial score inflation.
DIFFUSION IS FILE-TO-FILE ONLY, BY CONSTRUCTION.
claims.why: Code filters edges and hyperedge members to only those in file_ids set (nodes with kind in FILE_NODE_KINDS).

claims.text: On this repository, 2182 functions mention 227 distinct nominal types; if a type node may carry a diffusion step, then 'two functions that mention the same type' are two hops apart and 1,276,024 of the 2,379,471 possible function pairs become adjacent -- 53.6% of the complete graph, of which ``str`` alone contributes 939,135.
claims.why: These numbers are not present in the code chunk; they refer to external data.

claims.text: A channel that connects half the repository to itself does not rank anything; it normalises everything to the same score and the packer then falls back to node id order.
claims.why: Refers to behaviour of 'the packer' not in this chunk.

claims.text: So the type layers ship as a LENS: published for consumers that ask for them by name, never mixed into the score that decides what is read.
claims.why: No code in this chunk about LENS or score mixing.

claims.text: Turning them into a channel is a separate, gated lane whose precondition is the hub cap in ``index["types"]["coverage"]``.
claims.why: No reference to hub cap or index in this chunk.

claims.text: Filtering by node KIND rather than by relation NAME is deliberate: a name list would have to be edited every time a relation is added, and the edit that is forgotten is the one that reopens this.
claims.why: The code uses file_ids set derived from node.kind, not relation names.

observations.what: Prolongation.to_dict returns lists for tuple fields; consistent with serialization.
prolongate_scores uses queue pop(0) which is O(n) per operation; could be inefficient for large queues.
carry_temporal_scores iterates over sorted previous_scores items, which is deterministic but may be unnecessary.

In _relation_adjacencies, the 'direction' dict is updated per edge, but for hyperedges it is set to False unconditionally. If a relation appears both as edge and hyperedge, direction may be overwritten.
In _relation_adjacencies, the 'source_kind' dict is set for each relation; if a relation appears as both edge and hyperedge, the last processed one wins.
